videos.title: पहले यह जान लो: tissue समझने के जरूरी tools
videos.goal: आप cell के जरूरी हिस्से, division के basic words, body और plant के landmarks तथा transport, support और control के सीधे meanings को छोटे examples से समझ सकेंगे।
prerequisites_taught: Cell boundaries, organelles and plant–animal cell differences
Chromosomes, homologous pairs, chromatids, DNA replication and chromosome sets
Somatic cells, germ cells, gametes and fertilisation
Locations and roles of the named human organs, passages and skeleton
Diffusion, absorption, secretion and movement through walls or pores
Photosynthesis, food storage and the functions of structural biological materials
Physical meanings of tension, elasticity, pressure, buoyancy and insulation
Stimulus, nerve impulse, electrical signal and voluntary versus involuntary control
videos.opening_hook: एक ही शरीर में skin ढकती है, muscle खींचता है और nerve message पहुँचाती है—इनको समझने से पहले cell में क्या पहचानना जरूरी है?
videos.story_or_analogy: छोटे visual examples: कमरे की boundary से membrane और wall का फर्क, खिंचे rubber से elasticity, पानी पर तैरती चीज से buoyancy और गरम कपड़े से insulation। हर analogy की सीमा बताई जाएगी; यह बाहर का standard textbook-level support है।
videos.why_this_unit: Cell sketch, chromosome-pair sketch, body–plant locator और everyday physical examples से हर prerequisite को meaning तथा example मिलेगा। Replication में DNA बढ़ने और chromosome sets बदलने को अलग समझाया जाएगा; organelles या reproduction का पूरा पुराना chapter नहीं खुलेगा।

videos.title: Cells मिलकर tissue कैसे बनाते हैं?
videos.goal: आप division of labour से tissue, organ, organ system और organism का रिश्ता समझेंगे; mitosis–meiosis तथा plant–animal mitosis को book के सभी comparison criteria पर अलग कर सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: चोट के बाद skin ठीक होती है, लेकिन बच्चे बनने की प्रक्रिया में chromosome number आधा करना क्यों जरूरी होता है?
videos.story_or_analogy: अलग काम करने वाली teams मिलकर एक काम पूरा करती हैं—इससे division of labour समझेंगे, फिर cell से organism तक असली biological levels पर लौटेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Organisation के बाद cells की संख्या और उनके बनने का तरीका स्वाभाविक अगला सवाल है। दोनों comparisons में common basis, हर criterion के दोनों पक्ष और recap table आएँगे; DNA replication को chromosome-number doubling समझने की गलती साफ अलग की जाएगी।

videos.title: Animal tissues: शरीर में कौन क्या करता है?
videos.goal: आप 4 primary animal-tissue groups और book में दिए connective subgroups का tree बना सकेंगे तथा body diagram में tissue, जगह और काम जोड़ सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: आपके हाथ की skin, उसके नीचे की चर्बी, muscle और nerve—क्या ये सब एक ही तरह का tissue हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: हाथ से शुरुआत करके body diagram में बाहर से अंदर जाएँगे: covering, जोड़ने-सहारा देने वाला material, movement और message।
videos.why_this_unit: Classification tree को human-body locator के साथ पढ़ने से नाम जगह और function से जुड़ेंगे। हर group के समान परिचय-slots, मुख्य फर्क और छोटा memory cue होगा; बाद के videos इन्हीं branches को खोलेंगे। Figure के हर label को तय reading path से पढ़ेंगे।

videos.title: Epithelial tissue: covering की बनावट काम कैसे बदलती है?
videos.goal: आप epithelial sheets, barriers और gland formation समझेंगे; book के हर epithelial type को layers, shape, special feature, location तथा function से पहचानेंगे और drawings में true तथा apparent stratification अलग करेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: Skin को बचाव करना है और lung air sacs को gases पार होने देनी हैं—क्या दोनों जगह एक जैसी covering चलेगी?
videos.story_or_analogy: पतली exchange boundary और कई layers वाले protective cover की तुलना केवल thickness–function link समझाने के लिए होगी; हर निष्कर्ष असली tissue और book के location पर लौटेगा।
videos.why_this_unit: Sheet की common structure के बाद पूरा epithelial family tree आएगा। हर member समान slots में खुलेगा, फिर उसका drawing और location zoom होगा। अंत में confused pairs, side-by-side comparison, memory cue और matching-style check होगा।

videos.title: Connective tissue: matrix से support, storage और transport तक
videos.goal: आप matrix और fibres से connective tissues के गुण समझेंगे; book की सभी varieties, locations तथा atlas labels पहचानेंगे और subcutaneous fat वाले HPAS 2020 question का कारण सहित उत्तर दे सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: Blood बहता है और bone सख्त होती है—फिर दोनों connective tissue कैसे हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: Cells के आसपास का material बदलने से tissue का व्यवहार बदलता है। खिंचाव और वापस लौटने के छोटे demonstrations collagen तथा elastic fibres का फर्क खोलेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Common matrix–fibre structure से varieties की properties निकलेंगी। Overview के बाद हर member की structure, नाम का आधार जहाँ book देता है, feature, function और location पढ़ेंगे। Atlas में Haversian canals, canaliculi, chondrocytes, adipocytes और blood-cell labels पहचानेंगे; अंत में fat से कम heat loss की cause chain और supplied PYQ करेंगे।

videos.title: Muscle और nerve: खिंचाव, control और message का रास्ता
videos.goal: आप contraction से movement का रिश्ता, skeletal–smooth–cardiac muscle का पूरा comparison, tendon attachment और neuron में impulse की direction समझेंगे; striation को voluntary control का प्रमाण नहीं मानेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: आप हाथ उठाना रोक सकते हैं, लेकिन heartbeat को उसी तरह रोकने का आदेश क्यों नहीं दे सकते?
videos.story_or_analogy: हाथ मोड़ने का familiar action contraction, bone और tendon को जोड़ेगा। Neuron के लिए message का रास्ता केवल direction समझाने का सहारा होगा, biological mechanism का विकल्प नहीं।
videos.why_this_unit: पहले contraction का result, जगह और book में दिया mechanism; फिर 3-member muscle tree और हर member के समान structure–location–function slots होंगे। Comparison में branching, striation, nuclei और control अलग criteria रहेंगे। Cardiac question तथा tendon–ligament–cartilage distinction के बाद अलग neuron भाग में parts, synapse और arrows का reading path होगा। हर भाग का recap और अंत में एक closing recap होगा।

videos.title: Plant tissues का पूरा family tree
videos.goal: आप book के पूरे plant-tissue hierarchy को division के आधार सहित पढ़ सकेंगे और हर branch तथा member की जगह पहचान सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: पेड़ की बढ़ती नोक, मुलायम पत्ती और सख्त तना—इन अलग कामों को एक tissue map में कैसे रखेंगे?
videos.story_or_analogy: एक family tree में पहले बड़ी branches, फिर छोटी branches खोलेंगे; plant के familiar हिस्से हर branch का location anchor होंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Pages 1 और 8 के classification material को एक जगह जोड़ना जरूरी है। हर division का आधार, सभी named members, book में दिए distinguishing features, comparison और memory cue यहीं पढ़ेंगे। आगे के videos इसी tree की structures और mechanisms खोलेंगे, classification फिर से नहीं दोहराएँगे।

videos.title: Plant कहाँ बढ़ता है और cells specialised कैसे बनते हैं?
videos.goal: आप meristematic cells की features, apical–lateral–intercalary locations और length–girth effects समझेंगे; supplied statements हल करेंगे और differentiation से permanent tissue बनने की प्रक्रिया समझेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: पौधे की ऊँचाई बढ़ना और तने का मोटा होना—क्या दोनों का growth point एक ही जगह होता है?
videos.story_or_analogy: Plant sketch पर tip, base और side को अलग रंग से track करेंगे, ताकि location से growth effect निकले, केवल नाम याद न करना पड़े।
videos.why_this_unit: Meristem types को समान cell-feature, location और growth-effect slots में compare करेंगे। तुरंत supplied location question से गलत pairing जाँचेंगे। फिर dividing cell से specialised permanent tissue तक book की differentiation sequence, उसकी conditions और result पढ़ेंगे।

videos.title: Simple permanent tissues: storage, flexibility और strength
videos.goal: आप parenchyma और उसकी specialisations, collenchyma तथा sclerenchyma को structure से function तक समझेंगे; living contents, walls, spaces और locations पर compare करके buoyancy वाले questions हल करेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: मुलायम plant part, बिना टूटे मुड़ने वाला हिस्सा और सख्त seed covering—इनमें support का तरीका अलग क्यों है?
videos.story_or_analogy: मुड़ते plant part और कठोर covering को साथ देखकर flexibility तथा rigidity का फर्क खोलेंगे। Air spaces से floating का छोटा visual aerenchyma समझाएगा।
videos.why_this_unit: Simple permanent tissue की पूरी family एक साथ रहेगी। Overview tree के बाद हर member के समान slots, chlorenchyma–aerenchyma का function difference, wall thickening से support की cause chains और सभी comparative drawings पढ़ेंगे। सबसे confused pairs, full comparison table, memory cue और supplied practice अंत में होंगे।

videos.title: Xylem और phloem: components से transport समझें
videos.goal: आप complex tissue का मतलब, xylem और phloem के सभी components, उनके काम, labelled drawings और stem arrangement समझेंगे; living–dead exceptions तथा non-xylem component question सही करेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: जड़ों से पानी और पत्तियों से बना food बाकी plant तक पहुँचता है—क्या दोनों के लिए एक जैसी transport line होती है?
videos.story_or_analogy: Transport network का visual अलग materials और routes समझाने में मदद करेगा; storage तथा support करने वाले components को भी दिखाएँगे, ताकि हर component को केवल pipe न मानें।
videos.why_this_unit: Whole vascular bundle से components तक zoom करेंगे। Xylem और phloem members के समान structure–function slots, diagrams के सारे labels और stem में arrangement के बाद side-by-side comparison आएगा। Xylem parenchyma तथा phloem fibres जैसे exceptions स्पष्ट होंगे; printed transport shortcuts को absolute rules नहीं बनाएँगे।

videos.title: Plant की protective covering और gas exchange: questions खोलकर समझें
videos.goal: आप protective covering को wall material से और stomatal pore को guard cells से अलग कर सकेंगे; supplied questions के हर option को कारण देकर जाँच सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: पत्ती की covering बचाव भी करती है और gases का आना-जाना भी होने देती है—यह दोनों काम साथ कैसे होते हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: Covering में opening और उसे नियंत्रित करने वाले हिस्सों का visual इस्तेमाल करेंगे; pore और guard cells को एक ही चीज मानने की सीमा वहीं साफ होगी।
videos.why_this_unit: इन practice questions में नए explanatory links हैं, इसलिए इन्हें जल्दबाजी वाले final quiz में नहीं दबाएँगे। Plant से leaf covering और फिर pore–guard cells तक zoom, function से structure का रिश्ता और option-wise reasoning पढ़ेंगे। Book से बाहर जरूरी epidermis, wall-material या gas-exchange support को स्पष्ट रूप से बाहर का standard textbook explanation बताएँगे।

plan.chapter_flow: पहले 8 मिनट में सीधे जरूरी tools सीखेंगे। फिर organisation और cell division से animal-tissue tree बनेगा; epithelial, connective तथा muscle families अपने figures और questions सहित खुलेंगी, और neuron message की direction जोड़ेगा। इसके बाद plant-tissue tree से meristems, differentiation, simple permanent tissues और vascular tissues तक जाएँगे। आखिरी video protective covering तथा gas-exchange questions को समझाकर chapter बंद करेगा। सभी 35 concepts शामिल हैं; topic narration 100 मिनट और prerequisite सहित कुल 108 मिनट है। Topic videos prerequisites को अधिकतम 2 reminder beats में याद दिलाएँगे, दोबारा नहीं पढ़ाएँगे।

videos.title: पहले यह जान लो: tissue समझने के जरूरी tools

frame.process: Identify cell boundaries, internal contents and plant–animal differences.
frame.how: Move from membrane and wall to cytoplasm, nucleus and organelles.
frame.when: Before interpreting tissue cells and spaces.
frame.conditions: Typical plant and animal cells; specialised cells may differ.
frame.atmosphere: Two enlarged cells beside a familiar room-boundary image.

frame.process: Distinguish chromosomes, homologous partners, chromatids and sets.
frame.how: Follow DNA copying while keeping chromosome number separate from DNA quantity.
frame.when: Replication precedes division; copied chromatids later separate.
frame.conditions: Count chromosomes by centromeres; distinguish n from 2n.
frame.atmosphere: Paired instruction books and a simple chromosome diagram.

frame.process: Distinguish body cells, reproductive cell lineage and gametes.
frame.how: Connect meiosis with reduction and fertilisation with restoration of chromosome sets.
frame.when: Gamete formation precedes fertilisation.
frame.conditions: Use the human reproductive context.
frame.atmosphere: A body-cell example beside sperm and egg joining.

frame.process: Locate the organs and passages named in tissue descriptions.
frame.how: Trace digestive, respiratory, urinary, circulatory and nervous routes, then support structures.
frame.when: Before zooming from organs to their tissue linings.
frame.conditions: Distinguish neighbouring passages and ducts by their destinations.
frame.atmosphere: A simple labelled human-body outline.

frame.process: Locate plant organs, stem regions and section landmarks.
frame.how: Move from the whole plant to nodes, coverings and a stem cross-section.
frame.when: Before locating growth and transport tissues.
frame.conditions: Separate lengthwise position from outside-to-inside position.
frame.atmosphere: A potted plant beside a cut stem and split seeds.

frame.process: Distinguish diffusion, absorption, secretion and passage through openings.
frame.how: Use movement direction, concentration difference and selective barriers.
frame.when: During exchange, uptake and release.
frame.conditions: Movement depends on the barrier and the substance; pores do not imply unrestricted passage.
frame.atmosphere: An intestinal lining, a gland and a magnified plant wall.

frame.process: Connect food production, storage and biological materials with their jobs.
frame.how: Separate substances from the tissues containing or producing them.
frame.when: During photosynthesis, storage, support and protection.
frame.conditions: Materials have different properties and are not interchangeable tissue names.
frame.atmosphere: A green leaf, stored food and contrasting biological coverings.

frame.process: Interpret pulling, recoil, pressure, floating and reduced heat loss.
frame.how: Connect each physical term to a visible everyday effect.
frame.when: During stretching, contraction, pumping, floating and cooling.
frame.conditions: Analogies illustrate properties, not identical biological mechanisms.
frame.atmosphere: A rope, rubber band, pump, floating object and warm clothing.

frame.process: Distinguish a stimulus, its nerve signal and conscious versus automatic control.
frame.how: Trace detection to signalling and response.
frame.when: After a detectable change or during ongoing automatic activity.
frame.conditions: Biological electrical signalling is not metal-wire conduction; appearance does not determine control.
frame.atmosphere: Touching something hot, raising a hand and feeling a heartbeat.

beats.say: अपनी skin और चलती उँगली देखो—एक शरीर इतने अलग काम कैसे करता है? Tissue समझने से पहले cell, जगह और काम के जरूरी tools समझ लेते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Skin and moving finger beside a magnified cell.

beats.say: कमरे के दरवाजे जैसा cell में आना-जाना कौन सँभालता है? Cell membrane चीजों का आना-जाना control करती है। Plant cell में इसके बाहर सहारा देने वाली cell wall भी होती है; animal cell में wall नहीं होती।
beats.on_screen: Membrane in both cells; supporting wall outside the plant cell membrane.
beats.subtitle: कमरे के दरवाजे जैसा cell में आना-जाना कौन सँभालता है? Cell membrane चीजों का आना-जाना control करती है। Plant cell में इसके बाहर सहारा देने वाली cell wall भी होती है; animal cell में wall नहीं होती।
beats.voice: कमरे के दरवाजे जैसा cell में आना-जाना कौन सँभालता है? Cell membrane चीजों का आना-जाना control करती है। Plant cell में इसके बाहर सहारा देने वाली cell wall भी होती है; animal cell में wall नहीं होती।

beats.say: Cell में ये छोटे हिस्से दिखे? Organelles अलग काम करते हैं; cytoplasm अंदर का substance है, nucleus में DNA की instructions हैं। Vacuole storage करती है, plant cell में अक्सर बड़ी होती है; chloroplast food बनाने में मदद करता है, लेकिन हर plant cell में नहीं होता।
beats.on_screen: Label organelles, cytoplasm, nucleus, vacuole and chloroplast; root cell without chloroplasts.
beats.subtitle: Cell में ये छोटे हिस्से दिखे? Organelles अलग काम करते हैं; cytoplasm अंदर का substance है, nucleus में DNA की instructions हैं। Vacuole storage करती है, plant cell में अक्सर बड़ी होती है; chloroplast food बनाने में मदद करता है, लेकिन हर plant cell में नहीं होता।
beats.voice: Cell में ये छोटे हिस्से दिखे? Organelles अलग काम करते हैं; cytoplasm अंदर का substance है, nucleus में DNA की instructions हैं। Vacuole storage करती है, plant cell में अक्सर बड़ी होती है; chloroplast food बनाने में मदद करता है, लेकिन हर plant cell में नहीं होता।

beats.say: Intercellular space cells के बीच जगह है; extracellular material cells के बाहर का substance है। Multinucleate यानी एक cell में कई nuclei। अंदर, बाहर और boundary अलग पहचानो; कमरे की तुलना सिर्फ जगह समझाती है।
beats.on_screen: Distinguish cell contents, intercellular spaces and extracellular material; multinucleate cell inset.
beats.subtitle: Intercellular space cells के बीच जगह है; extracellular material cells के बाहर का substance है। Multinucleate यानी एक cell में कई nuclei। अंदर, बाहर और boundary अलग पहचानो; कमरे की तुलना सिर्फ जगह समझाती है।
beats.voice: Intercellular space cells के बीच जगह है; extracellular material cells के बाहर का substance है। Multinucleate यानी एक cell में कई nuclei। अंदर, बाहर और boundary अलग पहचानो; कमरे की तुलना सिर्फ जगह समझाती है।

beats.say: Instructions की किताब जैसी cell की जानकारी कहाँ है? DNA में; chromosomes DNA के organised packages हैं। Homologous pair में एक chromosome माँ से, दूसरा पिता से आता है; जानकारी के स्थान मिलते हैं, लेकिन versions अलग हो सकते हैं।

beats.say: Division से पहले DNA replication में copy बनती है। Copied chromosome की 2 sister chromatids centromere पर जुड़ी हैं: DNA दोगुना, chromosome संख्या अभी नहीं। गिनती centromeres से करो; अलग होने पर chromatids अलग chromosomes हैं।

beats.say: Skin cell और sperm का काम एक है? Somatic cells शरीर के सामान्य काम करती हैं; germ cells reproductive line की cells हैं। इंसान में sperm और egg gametes हैं; germ cell और mature gamete अलग stages हैं।
beats.on_screen: Somatic cell beside germ-cell lineage leading to gametes.

beats.say: खाना और साँस कहाँ जाते हैं? Gastrointestinal tract खाना food pipe से stomach और intestine तक पहुँचाता है; intestine nutrients लेती है। Respiratory tract हवा lungs तक लाता है; छोटे air sacs, यानी alveoli, blood से gases exchange करते हैं।

beats.say: Kidney tubules छोटी नलियाँ हैं, जो filtered fluid में बदलाव करती हैं। Urine ureter से bladder, फिर urethra से बाहर जाता है। Gland चीज बनाकर छोड़ती है; duct पहुँचाने की नली है, जैसे saliva को मुँह तक लाना।

beats.say: Skin बाहर का cover है; heart blood pump करता है, vessels उसे ले जाती हैं। Brain और spinal cord messages सँभालते हैं; bones सहारा देती हैं, joints उनके मिलने की जगह हैं। Tissue की जगह समझने के लिए पहले organ पहचानो।

beats.say: पौधे में पत्ती stem से कहाँ जुड़ी है? वह node है; 2 nodes के बीच internode। Petiole पत्ती का डंठल, leaf base जुड़ने वाला हिस्सा है; root tip जड़ का सिरा, shoot tip बढ़ते shoot का सिरा है।

beats.say: चना खोलने पर 2 seed leaves दिखती हैं; ये cotyledons हैं, इसलिए dicot। Maize monocot है, उसमें 1 cotyledon है। Plant में पहले organ, फिर लंबाई में जगह, फिर बाहर से अंदर का हिस्सा पहचानो।

beats.say: पतली lining exchange का रास्ता छोटा करती है; microvilli उँगली जैसे उभार (projections) हैं, absorption का area बढ़ाते हैं। Permeability गुजरने देने की क्षमता है; wall pits पतले हिस्से, sieve plate pores रास्ते, stomata leaf openings हैं। हर रास्ते से हर चीज नहीं गुजरती।

beats.say: हरी पत्ती food बनाती है, आलू जमा करता है—कैसे? Photosynthesis में chlorophyll light पकड़ने में मदद करता है; plant carbon dioxide और water से sugars बनाता है। Food transport या store होता है; starch और fat energy reserves हैं।

beats.say: रस्सी खींचने और rubber छोड़ने में फर्क? Tension खिंचाव का force है; elasticity पुरानी shape में लौटने की property। Muscle contraction force बनाता है, अक्सर muscle छोटा होता है; इससे खींचना या pumping होती है, लेकिन mechanism rubber जैसा नहीं।

videos.title: Cells मिलकर tissue कैसे बनाते हैं?

frame.process: Identify a tissue by its shared cellular function.
frame.how: Start with arm movement, explain cooperation, and test mere proximity.
frame.when: Before classifying tissues.
frame.conditions: Cells must cooperate in a common function.
frame.atmosphere: A student watching an arm move.

frame.process: Separate plant and animal tissues by constituent cells.
frame.how: Compare a leaf with a human arm.
frame.when: After defining tissue.
frame.conditions: Origin determines these two broad categories, not layer count or shape.
frame.atmosphere: A leaf and an arm shown side by side.

frame.process: Explain division of labour and reduced individual workload.
frame.how: Connect specialised jobs to coordinated organisation.
frame.when: Once cooperating cell groups are established.
frame.conditions: Specialisation does not remove essential cellular functions.
frame.atmosphere: Teams sharing jobs rather than each doing everything.

skipped_steps.why: The source provides no separate experimental evidence; the concrete example illustrates the mechanism.

frame.process: Locate cells, tissues, organs and systems within a whole organism.
frame.how: Zoom inward through a human digestive example, then assemble the labelled hierarchy.
frame.when: Following the explanation of organisation.
frame.conditions: The hierarchy describes multicellular organisation, not every organism.
frame.atmosphere: Nested views of a human, digestive system, stomach, tissue and cell.

frame.process: Distinguish mitosis and meiosis across all printed criteria.
frame.how: Pair each criterion and correct the chromosome-replication error.
frame.when: Compare starting cells, divisions, products and chromosome outcomes.
frame.conditions: Diploid products assume a diploid mitotic starting cell; reproductive generalisations need qualification.
frame.atmosphere: Two branching division diagrams with separate chromosome-set and DNA counters.

frame.process: Compare typical plant and animal mitosis.
frame.how: Contrast division apparatus, cytoplasmic separation and locations.
frame.when: After distinguishing mitosis from meiosis.
frame.conditions: Plant statements describe typical higher plants; distributed animal division does not mean every cell divides.
frame.atmosphere: A root-tip cell beside a dividing animal cell.

beats.say: Skin और sperm कैसे बनते हैं? Cell division के तरीके हैं mitosis और meiosis।

frame.process: Organise animal tissues into primary groups and nested subdivisions.

frame.conditions: Continuity requires close packing; the supporting boundary is described as usually present.
frame.atmosphere: An enlarged side section of an organ lining.

frame.process: An epithelial barrier maintains separation between body compartments.
frame.how: A continuous sheet prevents unrestricted contact while suitable linings permit exchange.
frame.when: The boundary remains functional while compartment contents differ.
frame.conditions: Barrier does not mean impermeable to every substance.
frame.atmosphere: Gut contents on one side of a lining and underlying tissue on the other.

frame.process: Epithelial specialisation produces gland cells and sometimes multicellular glands.
frame.how: Cells acquire secretion capability; a portion of the sheet may fold inward.
frame.when: The inward fold precedes the described multicellular gland arrangement; it is an occasional route.
frame.conditions: Neither secretion nor inward folding is universal to all epithelial cells.
frame.atmosphere: An epithelial sheet folding inward beside a visible secretion.

skipped_steps.why: The source provides no failed gland-formation mechanism; adding one would invent content.

frame.process: Epithelial architectures support exchange, absorption, secretion, protection and changing liquid volume.
frame.how: Layer number, surface-cell shape, renewal, keratin and surface projections modify the lining.
frame.when: Read each tissue from its free surface inward; renewal and bladder stretching introduce temporal changes.
frame.conditions: Site lists are not uniform whole-organ claims; ciliation and keratinisation require separate checks.
frame.atmosphere: Matched sections of lung, kidney, gut, gland ducts, skin and urinary passages.

frame.process: Compare apparent epithelial layering with genuine stratification.
frame.how: Inspect unequal cell heights and trace contact with the basement membrane.
frame.when: Check actual layers before interpreting nuclear rows.
frame.conditions: Respiratory mucus clearance applies to ciliated examples, not every pseudostratified lining.
frame.atmosphere: Adjacent simple columnar, pseudostratified and truly stratified sections.

frame.process: Recognise epithelial forms in two sets of perspective drawings.
frame.how: Inspect true layers, surface-cell proportions and projections in a fixed reading path.
frame.when: Read the four-panel figure first, then the seven-form comparison.
frame.conditions: The figures are comparisons, not process sequences; nuclear height alone cannot establish layers.
frame.atmosphere: Labelled epithelial blocks viewed from the side and above.

beats.say: Skin को बचाव करना है, lung air sacs को gases पार होने देनी हैं। क्या एक जैसी covering चलेगी? Epithelial tissue में बनावट से काम बदलता है।

beats.say: Tiles जैसी 1 पतली layer दिखे तो? Simple squamous है: flat cells की boundaries irregular हैं। Lungs के air sacs, blood vessels, capillaries और kidney की Bowman’s capsule में मिलता है; capsule यानी छोटी blood vessels के समूह के आसपास cup जैसी बनावट।

videos.title: Connective tissue: matrix से support, storage और transport तक

frame.process: Connective tissue binds, supports and packs body structures through cells and extracellular material.
frame.how: Read from the organ surroundings into spaced cells, gel and three fibre components.
frame.when: The framework supports structures continuously, including during pulling and movement.
frame.conditions: Fibre composition and arrangement determine tensile resistance, flexibility and recoil.
frame.atmosphere: Picture tissue beneath skin and around organs, then a magnified extracellular mesh.

frame.process: Support limits unwanted organ displacement while fibres determine mechanical behaviour.
frame.how: Attachments distribute forces; collagen resists pulling and elastic fibres recover after stretching.
frame.when: During body movement and when deforming forces are applied and removed.
frame.conditions: Normal movement remains possible; support does not mean absolute immobility.
frame.atmosphere: A moving body with supported internal organs and a pull-and-release demonstration.

frame.process: Matrix consistency is described as jelly-like, fluid, dense or rigid.
frame.how: Contrast gel, flowing plasma, closely packed fibres and rigid bone matrix.
frame.when: n/a: these are simultaneous material descriptions, not chronological stages.
frame.conditions: Descriptions need not be mutually exclusive; composition suits different functions.
frame.atmosphere: Four adjacent material demonstrations linked to familiar body tissues.

frame.process: Define connective tissues by support and connection of tissues and organs.
frame.how: Move from an attachment example to the definition, its evidence and a boundary test.
frame.when: After architecture and properties, before identifying examples.
frame.conditions: Shared identity does not require an identical matrix or consistency.
frame.atmosphere: An organised body whose parts are held in functional relationships.

frame.process: Identify cells and extracellular components in the general connective-tissue figure.
frame.how: Read upper-left cell, thick fibres and vessel, matrix annotation, then right-hand fibres and cells.
frame.when: Leader lines identify coexisting structures, not a timed sequence.
frame.conditions: Illustrative colours are not biological definitions; one vessel does not imply universal vascularity.
frame.atmosphere: The supplied description of the coloured connective-tissue field.

frame.process: Compare seven connective-tissue varieties by location, properties and function.
frame.how: Start from common organisation, compare location-function pairs, then resolve confused pairs.
frame.when: All varieties coexist in different body regions rather than developing in the listed order.
frame.conditions: A single organ may contain several tissues; support can be flexible, rigid or indirect through transport.
frame.atmosphere: A body map beside the book's tissue-location-function table.

frame.process: Read five atlas panels and distinguish their cells, matrix and channels.
frame.how: Follow blood, compact bone, hyaline cartilage, areolar tissue and adipose tissue.
frame.when: These are parallel examples, not stages in a process.
frame.conditions: Identify structures using panel context and leader lines, not proximity or colour alone.
frame.atmosphere: Five magnified drawings with each supplied label highlighted in turn.

frame.process: Answer the HPAS 2020 question about fat beneath skin.
frame.how: Select heat loss and distinguish insulation from storage, salt balance and the skin barrier.
frame.when: After adipose location, structure and function have been taught.
frame.conditions: The stem specifies underlying fat, not the outer skin surface.
frame.atmosphere: A four-option exam question beside a skin-and-fat cross-section.

videos.title: Muscle और nerve: खिंचाव, control और message का रास्ता

frame.process: Muscle tissue contains elongated force-producing cells called fibres.
frame.how: Contractile proteins inside each fibre interact to generate force.
frame.when: Examine tissue, then one fibre, then its internal machinery.
frame.conditions: A muscle fibre is a cell, unlike extracellular connective-tissue fibres.
frame.atmosphere: Picture an arm muscle enlarged to reveal long cellular units.

frame.process: Muscle activation raises force; relaxation reduces active tension.
frame.how: Internal contractile machinery responds to activation and its withdrawal.
frame.when: Force rises during activation and falls as activation subsides.
frame.conditions: Contraction need not visibly shorten the muscle; relaxation is not active pushing.
frame.atmosphere: Picture lifting and then lowering a held object.

frame.process: Muscle tissue is divided into skeletal, smooth and cardiac types.
frame.how: Compare cell form, location, function and control independently.
frame.when: Overview first, then members, contrast and mnemonic.
frame.conditions: Neither striation nor involuntary control identifies one type alone.
frame.atmosphere: Picture an arm, intestinal wall and heart.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle develops force transmitted to the skeleton.
frame.how: Long unbranched cylindrical cells contain multiple nuclei and repeated bands.
frame.when: Move from arm attachment to fibre outline and internal features.
frame.conditions: Bone attachment is typical; banding alone does not establish skeletal identity.
frame.atmosphere: Picture bending the forearm at the elbow.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle can lose force capacity during continued effort.
frame.how: Repeated work places demands on energy supply and activation.
frame.when: During sustained or intense effort; no fixed time is supplied.
frame.conditions: Fatigue varies with effort and muscle characteristics.
frame.atmosphere: Picture holding a heavy bag.

skipped_steps.why: The source contains no formula to construct.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle produces movement and stabilising posture.
frame.how: Transmitted pulls move bones or balance external forces.
frame.when: During limb movement and while holding a position.
frame.conditions: Force production need not produce visible movement.
frame.atmosphere: Compare bending an elbow with standing upright.

frame.process: Alternative names describe skeletal muscle from different viewpoints.
frame.how: Skeletal indicates association, striated appearance and voluntary usual control.
frame.when: After establishing its structure and function.
frame.conditions: The descriptors are not universally interchangeable categories.
frame.atmosphere: Attach three descriptive cards to an arm muscle.

frame.process: The illustration links skeletal fibres to arm movement.
frame.how: Read the fibre features and then the bent-arm view.
frame.when: After the structural and functional explanation.
frame.conditions: Colours are schematic; no connecting process arrow is printed.
frame.atmosphere: Parallel orange fibres beside an upper-arm illustration.

frame.process: Smooth muscle forms contractile cells in internal organ structures.
frame.how: Unbranched spindle cells have one central nucleus and no visible bands.
frame.when: Locate organ walls, trace one cell and inspect its centre.
frame.conditions: The named organs contain smooth muscle; they are not composed entirely of it.
frame.atmosphere: Picture gut and vessel walls and internal eye structures.

frame.process: Smooth muscle resists fatigue in normal sustained activity.
frame.how: Efficient tension maintenance supports long-duration internal work.
frame.when: During repeated or sustained organ activity.
frame.conditions: The book supplies a descriptive claim, not an experiment or numerical limit.
frame.atmosphere: Picture digestive activity continuing without conscious rest breaks.

skipped_steps.why: There is no formula in this item.

frame.process: Peristalsis transports contents along a hollow organ.
frame.how: A travelling contraction behind the contents coordinates with relaxation ahead.
frame.when: Repeatedly during digestive transport.
frame.conditions: Directed transport requires coordination, not just an isolated squeeze.
frame.atmosphere: Picture food travelling through the intestine.

frame.process: Smooth muscle is described as unstriated and involuntary.
frame.how: Separate microscopic appearance from conscious control.
frame.when: After explaining its cells and internal movement.
frame.conditions: Involuntary does not imply unstriated in every muscle.
frame.atmosphere: Compare gut activity with heartbeat during sleep.

frame.process: The smooth-muscle figure connects spindle cells with the intestine.
frame.how: Read the cell outline, central nuclei and absent stripes before the organ view.
frame.when: After teaching smooth-muscle features.
frame.conditions: The caption names the cell sketch, not the entire intestine.
frame.atmosphere: Orange spindle cells beside intestinal loops.

frame.process: Cardiac muscle forms the heart's contracting wall.
frame.how: Branched cylindrical striated cells form an interconnected arrangement.
frame.when: Locate the wall, inspect outline, nucleus and bands.
frame.conditions: The introductory pattern is one nucleus; the network is not one giant cell.
frame.atmosphere: Picture heart-wall cells enlarged beside the heart.

frame.process: Cardiac muscle sustains repeated normal beating without ordinary fatigue.
frame.how: Oxygen-dependent energy supply supports continued activity.
frame.when: Across repeated beats during waking and sleep.
frame.conditions: Adequate blood and oxygen supply remain necessary; no numerical endurance limit is given.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a heartbeat continuing through sleep.

frame.process: Heart-wall contraction and relaxation support ejection and filling.
frame.how: Contraction develops pressure; relaxation permits refilling.
frame.when: In coordinated recurring phases of each heartbeat.
frame.conditions: Effective repeated output requires filling as well as ejection.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a chamber alternately filling and pushing blood onward.

frame.process: Cardiac activity helps pump and distribute blood.
frame.how: Wall contraction raises pressure and drives blood into vessels.
frame.when: Repeatedly as circulation continues.
frame.conditions: Valves support direction; the vessel network carries blood to tissues.
frame.atmosphere: Picture blood reaching working muscles.

frame.process: Cardiac muscle combines striated appearance with involuntary activity.
frame.how: Classify appearance and control on separate axes.
frame.when: After teaching structure and pumping.
frame.conditions: Automatic rhythm does not require a conscious command for each beat.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a striped heart-muscle sketch beside a sleeping person.

frame.process: The cardiac illustration associates branched striped tissue with the heart.
frame.how: Read branches, bands, nuclei, caption and adjacent organ.
frame.when: After the cardiac explanation.
frame.conditions: Unlabelled white gaps are not identified chambers; colours are schematic.
frame.atmosphere: An orange branching tissue sketch beside a red heart.

frame.process: The table compares all three muscle types.
frame.how: Read location, function, appearance and control across types.
frame.when: After each type has been taught separately.
frame.conditions: Match combinations of properties rather than one word alone.
frame.atmosphere: A three-column comparison of arm, heart and visceral muscles.

frame.process: Three drawings visually reinforce the comparison table.
frame.how: Trace outline, branches, bands and nuclei in each.
frame.when: Immediately after the comparison.
frame.conditions: Illustrative colour does not identify tissue type.
frame.atmosphere: Three pink muscle drawings displayed side by side.

frame.process: Evaluate three statements about cardiac tissue.
frame.how: Check striation, control and shared features separately.
frame.when: After the muscle comparison.
frame.conditions: Identify the incorrect statement without inventing an option mapping.
frame.atmosphere: An exam statement-combination question.

frame.process: Select the muscle–bone attachment from four options.
frame.how: Contrast tendon, ligament and cartilage by their functions.
frame.when: After skeletal force transmission has been taught.
frame.conditions: A valid tendon option rules out None.
frame.atmosphere: Picture the elbow and the Achilles attachment behind the ankle.

frame.process: The neuron figure shows receiving structures, an outgoing axon and successive junctions.
frame.how: Read from the previous axon through the first neuron to the next neuron's dendrites.
frame.when: Follow the left-to-upper-right illustrated route.
frame.conditions: Separate cells remain distinct; the blue arrow shows electrical signalling along the axon.
frame.atmosphere: Two labelled neurons with an incoming previous axon and two circled synapses.

frame.process: A neuron receives input, conducts an impulse and can influence the next cell.
frame.how: Sufficient excitation initiates an axonal impulse; a typical chemical terminal releases transmitter.
frame.when: Reception precedes axonal conduction and terminal transmission.
frame.conditions: Not every input initiates an impulse; chemical synapses are not fused cells.
frame.atmosphere: Animate the route through the supplied neuron chain.

frame.process: Answer how neurons send messages to other cells.
frame.how: Distinguish conduction along an axon from transmission across a typical chemical synapse.
frame.when: After reading and animating the diagram.
frame.conditions: Present the chemical mechanism as typical, not universal.
frame.atmosphere: A short diagram-based explanatory exam answer.

videos.title: Plant tissues का पूरा family tree

frame.process: Classify plant tissues first by active division, then meristems by position and permanent tissues by cell-type composition.
frame.how: Trace parent–child connections, explain each member through structure, role and location, then contrast easily confused branches.
frame.when: Read from the root to major branches, tissue groups, specialised forms and visible transport components; this is not a time sequence.
frame.conditions: Meristematic cells actively divide; permanent cells are differentiated and generally not actively dividing. Simple and complex describe composition.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a growing plant with extending tips, flexible young stalks, hard supporting parts and transport pathways through roots, stems and leaves.

beats.say: नई डंडी बिना टूटे कैसे मुड़ती है? Collenchyma, Simple tissue का जीवित सदस्य, कोनों पर unevenly thickened दीवारों से लचीला सहारा देता है। पत्ती की डंडी और कई young dicot stems में बाहर के पास मिलता है, जिससे बढ़त बनी रहे।

beats.say: नारियल को कड़ा सहारा कैसे मिलता है? Sclerenchyma यानी मजबूत खोल जैसा Simple tissue। Lignin से मोटी दीवारें कड़ी होती हैं; cells आम तौर पर maturity पर dead होकर भी सहारा देते हैं। इसकी forms Fibres और Sclereids हैं।

beats.say: नाशपाती में सख्त दाने क्यों लगते हैं? Sclereids, Sclerenchyma के अक्सर छोटे, अलग-अलग आकार वाले cells हैं। मोटी-कड़ी दीवारें आसानी से दबती नहीं, इसलिए मुलायम फल में सख्त हिस्से महसूस होते हैं।

beats.say: जड़ का पानी पत्ती तक कैसे पहुँचेगा? Xylem, Complex tissue की पानी और minerals वाली pipeline है। इसमें दिखे Tracheids, Vessels यानी Tracheae, और Xylem parenchyma अलग काम सँभालते हैं; cropped list को पूरा मत मानना।

beats.say: बंद सिरों वाली नली से पानी आगे कैसे जाए? Tracheids, Xylem के लंबे, नुकीले सिरों वाले cells हैं। Maturity पर living contents नहीं रहते; पानी पास की दीवारों के pits से अगला रास्ता पकड़ता है।

beats.say: Pipe के टुकड़े जोड़ो तो क्या बनेगा? Xylem के Vessels, या Tracheae, ऐसे जुड़े elements की नलियाँ हैं। Tracheids से अलग, end walls की openings रास्ता जोड़ती हैं; mature elements dead और खोखले होते हैं।

beats.say: Pipeline के पास छोटा store कौन है? Xylem parenchyma यानी जीवित helper cells, जो सामान जमा करके बगल में पहुँचाते हैं। इसलिए सारा Xylem dead नहीं; helpers और नलियाँ साथ होने से यह Complex है।

beats.say: जाली वाले सिरों की food line कैसी होगी? Sieve tubes, Phloem के जुड़े जीवित elements हैं। Sieve plates के pores से तरल गुजरता है; maturity पर nucleus नहीं रहता, फिर भी helper cells के साथ ये जीवित रहते हैं।

beats.say: Tube के पास मददगार कौन है? Companion cells यानी साथ काम करने वाले जीवित Phloem cells। इनमें nucleus रहता है; flowering plants में ये कम cellular machinery वाले sieve-tube elements को काम चलाने में मदद देते हैं।

beats.say: Parenchyma आम तौर पर जीवित, thin-walled है; Collenchyma जीवित, uneven thickening से flexible support देता है। Sclerenchyma आम तौर पर maturity पर dead, lignified दीवारों से rigid support देता है; इसके fibers लंबे-पतले, Sclereids अक्सर छोटे, अलग आकार के हैं।

beats.say: नामों का trap देखो: Aerenchyma में air spaces; Chlorenchyma में photosynthesis वाले chloroplasts हैं। दोनों Parenchyma के नीचे हैं; Collenchyma अलग, flexible support वाला tissue है। Odd one out में spelling नहीं, parent branch पकड़ो।

beats.say: Xylem आम तौर पर पानी और minerals, Phloem organic food पहुँचाता है। Phloem हमेशा नीचे नहीं, ज़रूरत वाली जगह जाता है। सारे Xylem cells dead नहीं: parenchyma जीवित है; mature vessels dead, लेकिन Sieve tubes जीवित हैं।

frame.process: Locate three meristem positions and connect them to length or girth growth.
frame.how: Read the whole plant and enlarged insets from shoot tip to leaf base, stem side and root tip.
frame.when: These regions act during plant growth; the diagram is spatial, not a time sequence.
frame.conditions: Interpret arrows as growth directions and bands as schematic position markers.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a young plant becoming taller, extending roots and developing a thicker stem.

frame.process: Examine meristematic cells and the positions that organise their growth effects.
frame.how: Zoom from growing organs to cell outlines and internal compartments, then connect each location with its function.
frame.when: New cells are supplied during growth and can subsequently enlarge and specialise.
frame.conditions: Use several identifying features together; vacuole absence and beneath-bark placement are simplified cues.
frame.atmosphere: Move between a familiar seedling and magnified views of its growing tissues.

frame.process: Explain compact packing and the active cell-production role of meristems.
frame.how: Connect absent between-cell gaps to close packing, and repeated division to new building units.
frame.when: During active growth.
frame.conditions: Between-cell spaces differ from intracellular vacuoles; division is the principal role, not the only cellular activity.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a tightly packed workshop supplying new cells to a growing plant.

frame.process: Compare three tissue–location pairings.
frame.how: Check location, growth effect and restrictive wording side by side.
frame.when: After learning the growth regions and before choosing a statement combination.
frame.conditions: Treat beneath bark as the intended school-level location cue and scrutinise only.
frame.atmosphere: An examination table beside a labelled plant sketch.

frame.process: Select the correct supplied statement combination.
frame.how: Reject statement 1, retain statements 2 and 3, then match the printed options.
frame.when: After checking every statement independently.
frame.conditions: Read the options together with the preceding page's statements.
frame.atmosphere: A statement-combination practice question, with no verified examination provenance.

frame.process: Explain why cells adopt specialised roles and are called permanent.
frame.how: Connect the need for working tissues with specialisation and the usual loss of division.
frame.when: As newly produced cells mature.
frame.conditions: Permanent does not mean dead or absolutely incapable of renewed division.
frame.atmosphere: A growing plant needs completed working parts as well as new cells.

frame.process: Follow differentiation into characteristic shape, size and function.
frame.how: Track a meristem-produced cell through maturation and structural specialisation.
frame.when: After cell production, as daughter cells mature; no fixed interval is supplied.
frame.conditions: Distinguish division, enlargement and differentiation rather than treating them as synonyms.
frame.atmosphere: Follow one young shoot cell into a mature working tissue.

skipped_steps.why: The source supplies no specific differentiation failure mechanism or consequence to teach.

frame.process: Examine vacuole and wall features in mature plant cells.
frame.how: Move from the outer wall toward the central vacuole and connect each feature to its contribution.
frame.when: As cells develop mature structural features.
frame.conditions: Wall thickness varies; a large living vacuolar compartment is not universal in permanent tissues.
frame.atmosphere: A magnified mature living plant cell contrasted with specialised supporting cells.

frame.process: Connect permanent tissues with protection, support, storage and photosynthesis.
frame.how: Map each listed function onto a familiar plant part and explain division of labour.
frame.when: When differentiated tissues perform their specialised roles.
frame.conditions: The functions belong to the tissue family collectively, not necessarily to each cell.
frame.atmosphere: A whole plant with its covering, upright stem, stored food and green leaves.

skipped_steps.why: There is no numerical magnitude requiring a scale comparison.
The supplied fact contains no formula.

frame.process: Define simple permanent tissue and two specialisations of parenchyma.
frame.how: Distinguish one cell type, chlorophyll-containing cells and enlarged air-space arrangements.
frame.when: After differentiation; photosynthesis requires light and suitable living cells.
frame.conditions: Chlorophyll and prominent air spaces define different specialisations, not all parenchyma.
frame.atmosphere: A green leaf and a floating aquatic plant beside a soft plant part.

frame.process: Locate parenchyma and separate food production from food storage.
frame.how: Connect living packing and storage cells to several plant organs.
frame.when: Food can be stored for use when production is not occurring.
frame.conditions: Photosynthesis is conditional, not a universal property of simple tissues.
frame.atmosphere: A whole plant with roots, stem, leaves, flowers and fruits highlighted.

skipped_steps.why: These are qualitative facts with no numerical scale.

frame.process: Inspect the structure of parenchyma.
frame.how: Trace thin walls, variable cell shapes and gaps between neighbouring cells.
frame.when: Read the cell boundary before locating the gaps.
frame.conditions: No single cell shape is compulsory.
frame.atmosphere: A magnified group of living cells in soft plant tissue.

frame.process: Locate collenchyma in leaf stalks and dicot stems.
frame.how: Follow a leaf blade through its stalk into the stem.
frame.when: Flexible support matters as growing parts move and bend.
frame.conditions: Retain the source's dicot qualification.
frame.atmosphere: A leaf moving in wind on its stalk.

skipped_steps.why: No measurement or numerical scale is supplied.

frame.process: Inspect the living elongated cells of collenchyma.
frame.how: Trace close packing and uneven reinforcement at cell corners.
frame.when: Compare lengthwise shape before cross-sectional wall distribution.
frame.conditions: Very little space is not an absolute absence; elongation alone is not diagnostic.
frame.atmosphere: A magnified supporting region of a young leaf stalk.

frame.process: Explain support that allows plant parts to bend.
frame.how: Uneven primary-wall reinforcement supplies strength without strongly lignified rigidity.
frame.when: During bending of stalks, tendrils and climber stems.
frame.conditions: Photosynthesis requires chloroplasts; tissue support does not itself cause tendril coiling.
frame.atmosphere: A climber following a support and a stalk bending in wind.

frame.process: Locate and inspect mature sclerenchyma.
frame.how: Move from plant organs to lignified walls and the loss of living contents.
frame.when: Dead-cell descriptions refer to typical mature sclerenchyma.
frame.conditions: Long narrow shape describes fibres; other forms exist.
frame.atmosphere: Coconut husk, leaf veins and hard seed coverings.

frame.process: Explain rigid strength and the narrowing of the cell cavity.
frame.how: Wall deposition increases reinforcement while reducing the lumen.
frame.when: As supporting walls become heavily thickened.
frame.conditions: A narrow lumen is common; complete absence is not universal.
frame.atmosphere: A thick-walled supporting cell beside a hard protective covering.

frame.process: Read two comparative tissue plates and their labels.
frame.how: Read left to right, tracing boundaries, wall reinforcement and the position of spaces.
frame.when: Read lengthwise and cross-sectional views before comparing the second plate.
frame.conditions: Adjacent sketches are not developmental stages; the sclerenchyma pair shows two forms.
frame.atmosphere: Side-by-side labelled drawings rather than a sequence animation.

frame.process: Compare shape, walls, living contents, spaces, locations and functions.
frame.how: Use one criterion at a time across all three tissues.
frame.when: Apply the comparison after each tissue has been explained.
frame.conditions: Qualify photosynthesis, maturity, location claims and the table's simplified space descriptions.
frame.atmosphere: An aligned three-column reference table beside a stem cross section.

frame.process: Evaluate three proposed tissue-feature matches.
frame.how: Compare each claim with structural and functional evidence.
frame.when: After building the reference comparison.
frame.conditions: The climber statement is ambiguous; wall thickening alone does not establish lignin.
frame.atmosphere: A statement-combination practice question with evidence marked.

frame.process: Answer the supplied statement, lignin and buoyancy questions.
frame.how: Select using wall material and air-space architecture, while flagging ambiguous wording.
frame.when: At the end of the lesson.
frame.conditions: The first answer is apparently intended rather than unequivocal; aerenchyma is a tissue arrangement.
frame.atmosphere: Exam practice with distractors crossed out for stated reasons.

videos.title: Xylem और phloem: components से transport समझें

frame.process: Different cell types cooperate within complex permanent tissues; xylem contains four components.
frame.how: Identify conduits, associated parenchyma and fibres, then connect mature wall structure with their combined work.
frame.when: Describe conducting elements at maturity; this is structural organisation rather than a timed sequence.
frame.conditions: Component-level features must not be generalised to every cell in the tissue.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a stem transport network enlarged into its constituent cells.

frame.process: Complex tissues distribute supplies; xylem combines vertical conduction, lateral transfer, storage and support.
frame.how: Tubular elements provide longitudinal routes, parenchyma distributes water sideways and fibres reinforce the framework.
frame.when: Supplies move between separated plant regions as needed; no complete ascent-of-sap mechanism is taught.
frame.conditions: Tube shape provides a route, not by itself the force driving upward movement.
frame.atmosphere: Follow water from roots through a stem toward leaves and neighbouring tissues.

frame.process: Complex permanent tissues are grouped as xylem and phloem.
frame.how: Distinguish their cargo and associated roles while retaining their common multicellular organisation.
frame.when: Read permanent tissue, then complex tissue, then its two named kinds.
frame.conditions: These are tissue families, not single cell types or layer-count categories.
frame.atmosphere: Picture two coordinated supply networks within the same plant.

frame.process: The phloem component list contains five cell types.
frame.how: Separate conducting elements, companion cells, storage cells and supporting fibres.
frame.when: Introduce the whole list before following each component's role.
frame.conditions: The five-part list does not require sieve cells and sieve tubes to coexist in every plant.
frame.atmosphere: Zoom into the food-distributing tissue of a stem.

frame.process: Sieve-tube elements form a connected food-conducting route.
frame.how: Elongated cells meet at perforated end regions called sieve plates.
frame.when: Food-containing sap passes between adjoining elements during transport.
frame.conditions: Perforated does not mean every wall is freely open.
frame.atmosphere: Picture pipe sections connected by sieve-like end plates.

frame.process: Phloem distributes leaf-made food and contains a stated living-cell exception.
frame.how: Connect leaves with consuming regions and distinguish fibres from the other living components.
frame.when: Apply the fibre exception whenever evaluating a broad living-phloem statement.
frame.conditions: Support can depend on retained walls rather than living contents.
frame.atmosphere: Picture food moving from leaves toward a growing root.

skipped_steps.why: These are qualitative facts; no quantity exists to display to scale.

frame.process: Recognise tissue components in paired, isolated and grouped drawings.
frame.how: Read xylem first, then phloem, matching each leader line to its named structure.
frame.when: Move from the upper overview to the lower detailed views.
frame.conditions: Leader lines identify structures; the unclear tracheid pointer cannot justify a precise target.
frame.atmosphere: Use the supplied descriptions of the paired and boxed tissue drawings.

frame.process: Compare xylem and phloem across six printed criteria.
frame.how: Pair cargo, living condition, wall thickness, permeability, wall materials and support, qualifying shorthand claims.
frame.when: Compare one criterion at a time after component functions are understood.
frame.conditions: Do not turn dominant conducting-element features into universal tissue-wide rules.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a side-by-side table beside reinforced water tubes and living food pathways.

frame.process: Locate transport tissues within the illustrated stem and its enlargement.
frame.how: Move outside to centre, then enlarge the xylem–cambium–phloem region and read its arrows.
frame.when: Establish stem landmarks before interpreting the enlarged conducting structures.
frame.conditions: The red arrow indicates enlargement; downward phloem arrows show one possible transport direction.
frame.atmosphere: Picture the particular stem arrangement described in the source, not every possible stem.

frame.process: Identify the option that is not a xylem component.
frame.how: Read 'except', sort tissue membership and explain why parenchyma remains a valid xylem component.
frame.when: Attempt after studying both tissue families and their drawings.
frame.conditions: Companion cells belong to phloem, whereas the other three options occur in xylem.
frame.atmosphere: A four-option odd-one-out practice question.

beats.say: तो पत्ती पानी भी बचाती है और controlled openings से gas exchange भी कराती है। Exam में पूछी गई चीज पहचानकर पूरा clue मिलाओ; ‘thickest’ जैसी wording से समझा हुआ concept मत बदलना।
beats.on_screen: Protection + controlled exchange; read the complete stem before selecting.
